title: ISO Series, TQM, FSMS and ISO 22000:2005, Global Food Safety Management Systems
shortDescription: Quality and safety management systems: ISO 9001/22000 family, TQM tools and GFSI-benchmarked schemes. (Cross-reference: Exam Prep → ISO.)
genZNote: Syllabus says ISO 22000:2005, reality says 2018. Know both versions — it's the 'spot the outdated info' trap examiners love.

sections.heading: ISO 22000:2005 (Historical Syllabus Wording)
sections.body: ISO 22000:2005 "Food safety management systems — Requirements for any organization in the food chain" combined four elements: interactive communication, system management, prerequisite programmes and HACCP principles. Structure: clauses 4 FSMS, 5 Management responsibility, 6 Resource management, 7 Planning and realisation of safe products, 8 Validation, verification and improvement of the FSMS. It introduced the terms PRP and operational PRP and linked HACCP to ISO 9001-style management. The syllabus names this edition; ISO 22000:2005 was superseded by ISO 22000:2018, which adopts the High Level Structure (10 clauses), PDCA at two levels, risk-based thinking and clearer OPRP/CCP distinction. For application, remember the current standard is 2018 (see ISO lesson ISO 22000 for details).

sections.heading: TQM
bullets: Total Quality Management: organisation-wide, customer-focused continual improvement; pioneers Deming (PDCA, 14 points), Juran (quality trilogy), Crosby (zero defects).
Tools: PDCA, Pareto, fishbone, check sheets, control charts, 5S, Kaizen, Six Sigma.
Food application: complaints analysis, process capability, supplier management.

sections.heading: Global Food Safety Management Systems
bullets: GFSI (founded 2000) benchmarks schemes: BRCGS, SQF, FSSC 22000, IFS, Global G.A.P. (farm level), CanadaGAP.
Retailers require GFSI-recognised certification; audits are third party, annual or semi-annual with unannounced options.
Codex General Principles + HACCP form the technical basis of all these systems.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Food safety management standards combine PRPs, HACCP and management-system elements (ISO 22000), supported by TQM principles and GFSI-benchmarked global schemes.

highYieldFacts: ISO 22000 includes HACCP principles; HACCP is not an ISO standard.
commonTraps: Do not say ISO 22000:2005 is the current edition.

confusedTerms.distinction: HACCP is a hazard-control method; ISO 22000 is a full management system including HACCP principles.

questions.prompt: Which is not an element of ISO 22000:2005?
questions.explanation: The four elements are communication, system management, PRPs, HACCP.
It benchmarks private food safety schemes.
